'''Hellmut Fritzsche''' (20 February 1927 – 17 June 2018)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tucson.com/lifestyles/announcements/obituaries/fritzsche-hellmut-and-sybille-c/article_dbd70e04-7788-11e8-bb63-1b8bbfd75f86.html|title=FRITZSCHE, Hellmut and Sybille C|first=Classifieds Arizona Daily|last=Star|website=tucson.com|date=24 June 2018 |accessdate=26 June 2018}}</ref> was a German-born American physicist.

He came to the US on a one-year [[Smith–Mundt Act|Smith-Mundt fellowship]] in 1950/51. After receiving his [[Diplom]] in physics from the [[University of Göttingen]] in 1952 he returned to the US. He earned his [[Doctor (title)|Ph.D.]] from [[Purdue University]] in 1954 where in the same year he became Instructor and in 1955 [[Assistant Professor]]. In 1957 he moved to the [[University of Chicago]], where in 1963 he became a full professor and in 1996 retired. During this time he had children, Peter Fritzsche in 1959, Thomas Fritzsche in 1961, and Susanne Fritzsche in 1963, and later, Katja Fritzsche in 1970. During his career at the University of Chicago he was director of its Materials Research laboratory 1973–77 and chairman of its Physics department 1977–86. During his chairmanship he planned and oversaw the building of the Kersten Physics Teaching Center. For twenty five years Fritzsche served on the University of Chicago Advisory Committee for the [[Encyclopædia Britannica]] and during the last 7 years as its chairman. Fritzsche was a vice president and board member of [[Energy Conversion Devices, Inc.]] since 1969 and a member of the board of directors of United Solar Systems Corp. from 1993 to 2003. He had 3 grandchildren. Nina Fritzsche (b. 2006), Joshua Fritzsche (b. 2011) and Matteo Fritzsche (b. 2016)

== Research ==
Fritzsche trained 36 Ph.D. students. Some of the major accomplishments of his group were:
# The discovery and exploration of a new conduction process in semiconductors at very low temperatures: ''impurity conduction'', the hopping of charge carriers between the random distribution of [[impurity]] atoms. <ref name="Brown1995">{{cite book |title=Twentieth Century Physics |editor1=L. M. Brown|editor2=A. Pais|editor3=Sir B. Pippard |volume=III |pages=1330–1335 |publisher=AIP Press |location=New York |date=1995}}</ref>
# The elucidation of the [[metal-insulator transition]] of semiconductors.<ref name="Brown1995"/>
# The use of [[Doping_(semiconductor)#Neutron_transmutation_doping|neutron transmutation doping]] of some semiconductors: the transmutation of host atoms into doping atoms by the nuclear capture of thermal neutrons.
# The first use of [[synchrotron radiation]] as a light source resulting in a study of [[far ultraviolet]] spectra of solids and their electronic structure.<ref name="Margaritando2008">{{cite journal |title=The evolution of a dedicated synchrotron light source |author=Giorgio Margaritando |journal=Physics Today |volume=61 |issue=5 |pages=37–43 |date=May 2008|bibcode=2008PhT....61e..37M |doi=10.1063/1.2930734 |s2cid=67833433 }}</ref>
# The experimental and theoretical exploration of [[Amorphous silicon|amorphous semiconductor]]s discovered by [[Stanford R. Ovshinsky]] and their use in solid state electronic devices and [[solar panel]]s.<ref>{{cite book |title=The Science and Technology of an American Genius-Stanford R. Ovshinsky |editor=H. Fritzsche, B. Schwartz |publisher=World Scientific Publ. Co. |location=New Jersey, Singapore |date=2008}}</ref>

== Honors ==
* [[Humboldt Prize|Alexander von Humboldt Award]] 1985.{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}
* Honorary professor and member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], 1985.{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}
* Honorary professor, [[Nanjing University]] 1986.{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}
* Honorary professor, [[Beijing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics]], 1988.{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}
* Honorary Doctor of Science, Purdue University, 1988.
* [[Fulbright Scholarship]], professor at [[Tbilisi State University]], Georgia, USSR, 1988.{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}
* [[Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize]], 1989.
* Louis Block Professor of Physics, The University of Chicago, 1989.
* Scott Lecturer, Cambridge University, GB, 1990.{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}
* Fellow Commoner, Trinity College, Cambridge GB, 1992.{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}
* Fulbright Scholarship, Foundation for Research and Technology- Hellas, [[Heraklion]], Greece, 1992.{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}
* Stanford R. Ovshinsky Prize for Excellence in Non-Crystalline Chalcogenides 2004 <ref>{{cite journal |title=Stanford R. Ovshinsky Prize for Excellence in Amorphous Chalcogenides Past & Present |author=Mihai Popescu |journal=Phys. Status Solidi B |volume=249 |issue=10 |pages=1835–1836 |date=2012 |doi=10.1002/pssb.201200348|bibcode=2012PSSBR.249.1835P |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Publications ==
Fritzsche published 280 papers in scientific journals and wrote or edited 13 books. He held 15 [[US patent]]s.

== Selected writings by Fritzsche ==
* Editor: Amorphous Silicon and related materials, Parts A, B, World Scientific 1989
* Editor: Transport, correlation and structural defects, World Scientific 1990
* Editor with David Adler: Localization and metal-insulator transitions, Plenum Press 1985 (Vol. 3 a Festschrift for [[Nevill Francis Mott]])
* Electronic phenomena in amorphous semiconductors, Annual Review of Material Science, Vol.2, 1972, pp.&nbsp;697–744
* Editor with Brian Schwartz: Stanford R. Ovshinsky – the science and technology of an American genius, World Scientific 2008
